card.name: "It is" before unknown or uncertain findings
card.fires_on: The word "is" (rarely "more") right after a subject like "It" or a finding, where the sentence is about to say something is unknown, possible, or considered a certain way. Seen in study results and warnings.

modes.label: It is unknown
modes.description: "is" after "It" when a statement about whether findings apply or extend is coming.
modes.example: It<< is>> unknown whether these findings apply to younger

modes.label: Is after a risk or finding
modes.description: "is" following a noun phrase describing a result, before a judgment such as considered or consistent with.
modes.example: The increased risk of asthma-related death<< is>> considered a class effect of LABAs,

modes.label: Even more
modes.description: The word "more" in "Even more" introducing a further point of concern.
modes.example: Even<< more>>, the popcorn butter flavorant can pass

card.writes: It pushes toward words meaning about or regarding, such as concerning, regarding and concern.
card.plain: It fires on the small word "is" when a sentence is about to comment on what is known or worrying about a finding.
